```{python}
#| label: helpers
def load_psd_csv(path):
    """Split a saved normalized-PSD table into (psd_matrix, freqs, metadata).

    Frequency columns are numeric-named; everything else is metadata. The index
    is the channel name.
    """
    df = pd.read_csv(path, index_col=0)
    num_cols = [c for c in df.columns if str(c).replace(".", "", 1).isdigit()]
    freqs = np.array([float(c) for c in num_cols])
    psd = df[num_cols].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    meta = df[[c for c in df.columns if c not in num_cols]].copy()
    meta.index = df.index
    return psd, freqs, meta


def assign_band(cf, bands=EEG_BANDS):
    """Canonical band name for a peak centre frequency; None if outside all bands.

    Half-open [lo, hi) except the last band, which is closed [lo, hi].
    """
    for i, b in enumerate(bands):
        if (b.lo <= cf < b.hi) or (i == len(bands) - 1 and cf == b.hi):
            return b.name
    return None


def channel_fit_quality(fg, channel_names, dataset):
    """Per-channel goodness of fit: R² and MSE of the full log-power model.

    R² is specparam's own ``gof_rsquared``; MSE is the mean squared residual in
    log10-power space, reconstructing the model from the fitted aperiodic and
    peak parameters (same construction as the BIC build doc).
    """
    freqs = np.asarray(fg.data.freqs, dtype=float)
    rows = []
    for i, (channel, result) in enumerate(zip(channel_names, fg.results)):
        ap = fg.modes.aperiodic.func(freqs, *np.asarray(result.aperiodic_fit, dtype=float))
        peak_params = np.asarray(result.peak_fit, dtype=float).ravel()
        peak = fg.modes.periodic.func(freqs, *peak_params) if peak_params.size else 0.0
        residual = np.asarray(fg.data.power_spectra[i], dtype=float) - (ap + peak)
        rows.append(
            {
                "channel": channel,
                "dataset": dataset,
                "gof_rsquared": result.metrics.get("gof_rsquared", np.nan),
                "mse_log10": float(np.mean(residual**2)),
            }
        )
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def fit_and_extract_peaks(path, dataset, mode):
    """Fit the selected aperiodic mode and return a tidy peak table.

    One row per fitted peak: channel, dataset, Region name, Lobe, mni_y, CF, PW,
    BW, band. Also returns the per-channel metadata (the prevalence denominator)
    and a per-channel fit-quality table (R², MSE).
    """
    psd, freqs, meta = load_psd_csv(path)
    meta = meta.assign(
        dataset=dataset,
        region=meta["Region name"].astype(str).str.strip("'"),
        mni_y=pd.to_numeric(meta["mni_y"], errors="coerce"),
    )

    fg = SpectralGroupModel(**SPECPARAM_SETTINGS, aperiodic_mode=mode, verbose=False)
    fg.fit(freqs, psd, freq_range=list(FREQ_RANGE), n_jobs=1)

    peaks = fg.get_params("peak")  # (n_peaks, 4): [CF, PW, BW, ID]
    peaks = np.atleast_2d(peaks)
    peak_df = pd.DataFrame(peaks, columns=["CF", "PW", "BW", "ID"])
    peak_df["ID"] = peak_df["ID"].astype(int)
    peak_df["channel"] = meta.index.to_numpy()[peak_df["ID"].to_numpy()]
    peak_df["band"] = peak_df["CF"].map(assign_band)
    peak_df = peak_df.dropna(subset=["band"])

    keep = ["region", "Lobe", "mni_y", "dataset"]
    peak_df = peak_df.merge(meta[keep], left_on="channel", right_index=True, how="left")
    channels = meta[["region", "Lobe", "mni_y", "dataset"]].reset_index(names="channel")
    quality = channel_fit_quality(fg, meta.index.astype(str), dataset)
    return peak_df, channels, quality


def channel_band_table(peak_df, channels, bands=EEG_BANDS):
    """One row per (channel, band): has_peak and the band's modelled power.

    modelled_power is the highest peak's amplitude in the band; channels with no
    peak in the band get has_peak=False and modelled_power=NaN (the amplitude is
    undefined where nothing was detected).
    """
    band_names = [b.name for b in bands]
    best = (
        peak_df
        .sort_values("PW", ascending=False)
        .drop_duplicates(["channel", "band"])
        .set_index(["channel", "band"])["PW"]
    )
    grid = (
        channels
        .assign(key=1)
        .merge(pd.DataFrame({"band": band_names, "key": 1}), on="key")
        .drop(columns="key")
    )
    grid["modelled_power"] = grid.set_index(["channel", "band"]).index.map(best)
    grid["has_peak"] = grid["modelled_power"].notna()
    return grid


def region_prevalence_power(channel_band):
    """Collapse channels to regions: prevalence and median modelled power per band."""
    g = channel_band.groupby(["dataset", "region", "Lobe", "band"], observed=True)
    out = g.agg(
        n_channels=("channel", "nunique"),
        prevalence=("has_peak", "mean"),
        # amplitude where detected (separates amplitude from detection rate)
        median_power=("modelled_power", "median"),
        mni_y=("mni_y", "mean"),
    ).reset_index()
    return out


def clustering_region_order(region_info_csv=REGION_INFO_CSV, lobe_order=LOBE_ORDER):
    """Top→bottom region order matching the clustering-result heatmaps.

    Regions are grouped into lobe blocks in ``lobe_order`` (Insula, absent from
    that tuple, falls to the end); within a lobe they keep the atlas region
    numbering. This reproduces ``pesco.experimental.plotting`` row order.
    """
    info = pd.read_csv(region_info_csv)
    info["region"] = info["Region name"].astype(str).str.strip().str.strip("'")
    info["lobe"] = info["Lobe"].astype(str).str.strip().str.strip("'")
    rank = {lo: i for i, lo in enumerate(lobe_order)}
    info["__lobe_rank"] = info["lobe"].map(lambda l: rank.get(l, len(lobe_order)))
    # stable sort keeps the atlas region order (encounter order) within each lobe
    return info.sort_values("__lobe_rank", kind="stable")["region"].tolist()


def region_lobe_map(region_info_csv=REGION_INFO_CSV):
    """Map each display region name to its lobe (for colouring y-axis labels)."""
    info = pd.read_csv(region_info_csv)
    region = info["Region name"].astype(str).str.strip().str.strip("'")
    lobe = info["Lobe"].astype(str).str.strip().str.strip("'")
    return dict(zip(region, lobe))


def save_lobe_colored(plot, paths, dpi=150):
    """Draw a heatmap, colour its y-axis region labels by lobe, save, return the figure.

    plotnine themes one colour across all tick labels, so the per-lobe colouring
    of the clustering heatmaps is applied on the drawn matplotlib axes instead.
    """
    fig = plot.draw(show=False)
    lobe_of = region_lobe_map()
    for ax in fig.axes:
        for label in ax.get_yticklabels():
            lobe = lobe_of.get(label.get_text())
            if lobe:
                label.set_color(LOBE_TEXT_COLORS.get(lobe, "black"))
    for path in paths:
        fig.savefig(path, dpi=dpi, bbox_inches="tight")
    return fig


def ordered_region_band(region_power):
    """Add ordered categoricals: band labels (δ→γ) and clustering-style regions.

    Returns the dataframe plus the y-axis category order (reversed lobe order, so
    the first lobe block — Occipital — sits at the top of the tile plot).
    """
    d = region_power.copy()
    # top→bottom = clustering order; plotnine draws the first category at the
    # bottom, so reverse to put Occipital at the top.
    y_order = list(reversed(clustering_region_order()))
    d["region"] = pd.Categorical(d["region"], categories=y_order, ordered=True)
    d["band_label"] = pd.Categorical(
        d["band"].map(BAND_LABELS), categories=BAND_LABEL_ORDER, ordered=True
    )
    d["dataset"] = pd.Categorical(
        d["dataset"], categories=["iEEG atlas", "source HD-EEG"], ordered=True
    )
    return d, y_order
```

```{python}
peak_tables, channel_tables, quality_tables = [], [], []
for dataset, path in INPUT_CSV.items():
```

```{python}
#| label: pairing
def pair_region_band(region_power, value, x="iEEG atlas", y="source HD-EEG"):
    """Wide table region×band with the value from each modality, + Spearman per band."""
    wide = region_power.pivot_table(
        index=["region", "band"], columns="dataset", values=value, observed=True
    ).reset_index()
    wide = wide.rename(columns={x: "x_value", y: "y_value"}).dropna(
        subset=["x_value", "y_value"]
    )
    wide["band_label"] = pd.Categorical(
        wide["band"].map(BAND_LABELS), categories=BAND_LABEL_ORDER, ordered=True
    )
    rows = []
    for name in BAND_ORDER:
        sub = wide[wide["band"] == name]
        if len(sub) >= 3:
            rho, p = stats.spearmanr(sub["x_value"], sub["y_value"])
        else:
            rho, p = np.nan, np.nan
        rows.append({"band": name, "spearman_rho": rho, "p_value": p, "n": len(sub)})
    return wide, pd.DataFrame(rows)


prevalence_pairs, prevalence_rho = pair_region_band(region_power, "prevalence")
```

## Methods

### Per-band peak prevalence and modelled power

For each channel, we assigned the parameterised specparam peaks to canonical bands by their centre frequency. Peak prevalence in a region is the proportion of channels in that region with at least one peak in a given band.

We also kept the parameters of the fitted peaks: centre frequency, amplitude, and bandwidth. We take the amplitude of the highest peak within a band as the modelled power of that band's rhythm, following @castanheira2025QuantifyingRhythmicArrhythmic, who retain the highest-amplitude Gaussian when more than one peak falls in the band. Channels with no fitted peak in a band are assigned a modelled power of zero rather than dropped. This keeps the channel set fixed across bands, but it leaves a spike of zeros in the distribution, so band-power comparisons use rank-based statistics. @castanheira2025QuantifyingRhythmicArrhythmic show in simulation that modelled power recovers oscillatory amplitude almost independently of the aperiodic exponent, whereas the residual obtained by subtracting the aperiodic fit (next subsection) inherits the error of that fit. We therefore carry modelled power as the periodic measure we trust by default, and the subtraction residual as the comparison.

Modelled power exists only where specparam fits a peak, so the per-band prevalence above is also a fit-success rate. We report it separately for each modality. <!-- If the algorithm fits peaks less often in the source-reconstructed HD-EEG than in the iEEG, a difference in modelled power between modalities could reflect differential peak detection rather than a difference in the rhythm itself, and we read the modelled-power comparison with that rate in hand. -->

Assigning peaks to fixed canonical bands by centre frequency is sensitive to peaks that sit near a band edge [@castanheira2025QuantifyingRhythmicArrhythmic], and source reconstruction can shift the estimated peak frequency. We therefore also report the distribution of peak centre frequencies per region per modality, and compare the regional dominant peak frequency across modalities directly, without binning.

## Results


#### Per-band peak prevalence from specparam

Once oscillations are modelled explicitly, peak prevalence — the fraction of a region's channels carrying at least one fitted peak in a band — diverges sharply between modalities (@fig-peak-prevalence). Source HD-EEG is dominated by alpha: mean prevalence across regions is 0.63 in alpha but only 0.11 in theta, 0.05 in gamma and 0.01 in delta. The iEEG atlas is broader, with substantial beta (0.40), gamma (0.26) and alpha (0.24) prevalence. The difference map (HD − iEEG) is strongly positive in alpha — HD detects alpha peaks far more often, especially in posterior regions — and negative across beta and gamma, where iEEG detects high-frequency peaks that the source fit does not recover.

Cross-modal agreement of the regional prevalence *pattern* (Spearman across the 38 bilateral regions) is confined to the low and mid bands: alpha $\rho = 0.60$ and beta $\rho = 0.47$, against delta $\rho = 0.04$, theta $\rho = -0.07$ and gamma $\rho = -0.25$ (@fig-prevalence-scatter). In alpha the points sit above the identity line — HD detects alpha in more regions than iEEG — yet the two modalities still rank regions consistently. This mirrors the uncorrected relative-band-power result (alpha strongest, gamma anti-correlated), now with the aperiodic background modelled out rather than carried in the power.

Because modelled power exists only where a peak is fitted, prevalence is also the peak-detection rate and must be read alongside the amplitude and centre-frequency descriptors. Mean peaks per channel were similar across modalities (iEEG 1.45, HD 1.37 under the main settings), but 99.7% of iEEG channels passed the $R^2 > 0.9$ screen against only 74.0% of HD channels, with the missing HD peaks concentrated in the high-frequency bands where the source spectrum is flattest.

```{python}
def plot_prevalence_difference(prevalence_pairs, region_order):
    d = prevalence_pairs.copy()
    d["diff"] = d["y_value"] - d["x_value"]  # HD − iEEG
    d["region"] = pd.Categorical(d["region"], categories=region_order, ordered=True)

        ggplot(d, aes("band_label", "region", fill="diff"))
        + geom_tile(color="white", size=0.3)
        + scale_fill_gradient2(
            low="#B2182B", mid="white", high="#2166AC",
            midpoint=0, limits=(-lim, lim), name="HD − iEEG",
        )
        + labs(
            x="band", y="",
            title="Prevalence difference (source HD-EEG − iEEG atlas)",
        )
        + theme_bw()
        + theme(
            figure_size=(5.5, 9),
            axis_text_y=element_text(size=6),
            plot_title=element_text(size=11),
```

```{python}
#| label: build-prevalence-scatter
def plot_agreement_scatter(pairs, rho, value_name, title):
    strip = {
        BAND_LABELS[r["band"]]: f"{BAND_LABELS[r['band']]}\nρ={r['spearman_rho']:.2f}"
        for _, r in rho.iterrows()
    }
    d = pairs.copy()
    d["panel"] = pd.Categorical(
        d["band_label"].astype(str).map(strip),
        categories=[strip[lbl] for lbl in BAND_LABEL_ORDER],
        ordered=True,
    )
    color = {strip[BAND_LABELS[n]]: BAND_COLORS[n] for n in BAND_ORDER}
    return (
        ggplot(d, aes("x_value", "y_value"))
        + geom_abline(slope=1, intercept=0, linetype="dashed", color="#999999")
        + geom_point(aes(fill="panel"), size=2.2, alpha=0.8, stroke=0, show_legend=False)
        + scale_fill_manual(values=color, guide=None)
        + facet_wrap("panel", nrow=1)
        + labs(
            x=f"iEEG atlas\n{value_name}", y=f"source HD-EEG\n{value_name}",
            title=title,
        )
        + theme_classic()
        + theme(
            figure_size=(15, 3.3),
            panel_spacing=0.04,
            strip_background=element_blank(),
        )
    )


prevalence_scatter = plot_agreement_scatter(
    prevalence_pairs, prevalence_rho, "peak prevalence",
    "Cross-modal prevalence agreement (one point per region)",
)
for ext in ("pdf",):
    prevalence_scatter.save(
        fig_dir / f"peak_prevalence_agreement_scatter.{ext}",
        width=15, height=3.3, dpi=150, verbose=False,
    )
prevalence_scatter
```

**Modelled power.** <!-- REVIEW: "tells the same story in amplitude that prevalence tells in detection" — LLM-style parallelism/cliché. State the finding directly. -->
The amplitude of the highest peak per band (median across the channels that carry a peak) tells the same story in amplitude that prevalence tells in detection: posterior alpha carries the largest modelled power in HD-EEG, while in iEEG the amplitude is spread across beta in frontal and central regions (@fig-modelled-power).

**Centre frequency and dominant rhythm.** Because canonical-band assignment is sensitive to peaks near a band edge, we also examined the fitted centre frequencies directly. The HD-EEG centre-frequency distribution is a sharp alpha mode at ~10 Hz, sitting squarely against the 8 and 13 Hz band edges, whereas iEEG peaks are broadly distributed with an additional high-gamma cluster near 70 Hz (@fig-centre-freq). The per-region dominant peak frequency — the centre frequency of the single highest-amplitude peak — is alpha-locked across almost all regions in HD-EEG but scatters into beta and gamma for several frontal and temporal regions in iEEG (@fig-dominant-dumbbell). The full per-region distribution of peak frequencies confirms a narrow posterior alpha ridge in HD against broader, multimodal iEEG ridges (@fig-region-ridges).

```{python}
#| label: build-centre-frequency
def plot_centre_frequency(all_peaks):
    edges = band_edges()  # band lower edges + final upper edge
    d = all_peaks.assign(
        dataset=pd.Categorical(
            all_peaks["dataset"],
            categories=["iEEG atlas", "source HD-EEG"], ordered=True,
        )
    )
    return (
        ggplot(d, aes("CF", fill="dataset"))
        + geom_vline(xintercept=edges, linetype="dashed", color="#999999", size=0.4)
        + geom_density(alpha=0.45, color="none")
        + scale_x_continuous(breaks=[1, 4, 8, 13, 30, 50, 80])
        + labs(
            x="peak centre frequency (Hz)", y="density", fill="",
            title="Fitted peak centre frequencies vs canonical band edges",
        )
        + theme_bw()
        + theme(figure_size=(8, 3.5), plot_title=element_text(size=11))
    )


cf_fig = plot_centre_frequency(all_peaks)
for ext in ("pdf",):
    cf_fig.save(
        fig_dir / f"peak_centre_frequency_distribution.{ext}",
        width=8, height=3.5, dpi=150, verbose=False,
    )
cf_fig
```

```{python}
#| label: build-dominant-dumbbell
def region_dominant_frequency(all_peaks):
    """Centre frequency of the highest-PW peak per (modality, region)."""
    idx = all_peaks.groupby(["dataset", "region"], observed=True)["PW"].idxmax()
    return all_peaks.loc[idx, ["dataset", "region", "Lobe", "CF", "PW"]].reset_index(
        drop=True
    )


def plot_dominant_frequency_dumbbell(all_peaks):
    dom = region_dominant_frequency(all_peaks)
    y_order = list(reversed(clustering_region_order()))
    dom["region"] = pd.Categorical(dom["region"], categories=y_order, ordered=True)
    dom["dataset"] = pd.Categorical(
        dom["dataset"], categories=["iEEG atlas", "source HD-EEG"], ordered=True
    )
    # Wide form for the connecting segment (regions present in both modalities).
    wide = (
        dom.pivot_table(index="region", columns="dataset", values="CF", observed=True)
        .dropna(subset=["iEEG atlas", "source HD-EEG"])
        .reset_index()
    )
    wide["region"] = pd.Categorical(wide["region"], categories=y_order, ordered=True)
    return (
        ggplot()
        + geom_vline(xintercept=band_edges(), linetype="dashed", color="#cccccc", size=0.3)
        + geom_segment(
            wide,
            aes(x="iEEG atlas", xend="source HD-EEG", y="region", yend="region"),
            color="#bdbdbd",
            size=1.5,
        )
        + geom_point(dom, aes("CF", "region", color="dataset"), size=3, stroke=0)
        + scale_color_manual(values=DATASET_COLORS, name="")
        + scale_x_continuous(breaks=[1, 4, 8, 13, 30, 50, 80])
        + labs(
            x="dominant peak frequency (Hz)",
            y="",
            title="Dominant peak frequency per region (highest-amplitude peak)",
        )
        + theme_bw()
        + theme(
            figure_size=(8, 9),
            axis_text_y=element_text(size=6),
            plot_title=element_text(size=11),
            legend_position="top",
        )
    )


dumbbell_fig = save_lobe_colored(
    plot_dominant_frequency_dumbbell(all_peaks),
    [
        fig_dir / f"dominant_frequency_dumbbell.{ext}"
        for ext in ("pdf",)
    ],
)
dumbbell_fig
```

```{python}
#| label: build-region-ridges
def plot_region_frequency_ridges(
    all_peaks,
    binwidth=1.0,
    scale=1.2,
    alpha=0.6,
    title="Per-region peak-frequency distribution (histogram ridgeline)",
):

    lobe_of = region_lobe_map()
    d = all_peaks.assign(lobe=all_peaks["region"].map(lobe_of))
    # Discrete y: plotnine draws the first category at the bottom, so reverse the
    # clustering order to put Occipital on top.
    d["region"] = pd.Categorical(
        d["region"], categories=list(reversed(region_order)), ordered=True
    )
    d["dataset"] = pd.Categorical(
        d["dataset"], categories=["iEEG atlas", "source HD-EEG"], ordered=True
    )
    d["lobe"] = pd.Categorical(
        d["lobe"], categories=list(LOBE_ORDER) + ["Insula"], ordered=True
```

Pooling all regions, <!-- REVIEW: "makes the contrast immediate" — LLM flourish. Cut or replace with neutral "shows". -->
the joint distribution of peak amplitude and centre frequency (@fig-size-freq) makes the contrast immediate: HD-EEG peaks form one dense high-amplitude alpha mode at ~10 Hz with a sparse low-amplitude tail above it, whereas iEEG peaks spread along the frequency axis at moderate amplitude, with a distinct beta/low-gamma body and a high-gamma cluster near 70 Hz.

Jointly resolving peak amplitude and centre frequency per lobe (@fig-size-freq-lobe) confirms that the two descriptors are not redundant. In HD-EEG the per-channel peak density concentrates into a single tall alpha column in occipital and parietal lobes — high amplitude at ~10 Hz — and thins sharply elsewhere. In iEEG the density is spread along the frequency axis at moderate amplitude, with frontal and temporal lobes carrying beta and low-gamma peaks that have no HD-EEG counterpart. Normalising to peaks per channel makes the lobes comparable despite their different channel counts, and shows the cross-modal divergence is one of *where in the spectrum* rhythms occur, not merely how strong they are.

```{python}
#| label: build-size-frequency-lobe
LOBE_FACET_ORDER = list(LOBE_ORDER) + ["Insula"]


def plot_peak_size_frequency_by_lobe(all_peaks, channel_band, bins=30):
    # Channels per (modality, lobe) is the normalisation denominator; taken from
    # the full channel list so channels with no peak still count.
    n_channels = (
        channel_band.assign(
            Lobe=channel_band["Lobe"].astype(str).str.strip().str.strip("'")
        )
        .groupby(["dataset", "Lobe"], observed=True)["channel"]
        .nunique()
        .rename("n_channels")
        .reset_index()
    )
    d = all_peaks.assign(
        Lobe=all_peaks["Lobe"].astype(str).str.strip().str.strip("'")
    ).merge(n_channels, on=["dataset", "Lobe"], how="left")
    d["weight"] = 1.0 / d["n_channels"]
    d["Lobe"] = pd.Categorical(d["Lobe"], categories=LOBE_FACET_ORDER, ordered=True)
    d["dataset"] = pd.Categorical(
        d["dataset"], categories=["iEEG atlas", "source HD-EEG"], ordered=True
    )
    return (
        ggplot(d, aes("CF", "PW"))
        + geom_bin2d(aes(weight="weight"), bins=bins)
        + geom_vline(xintercept=band_edges(), linetype="dashed", color="#999999", size=0.25)
        + scale_fill_cmap(cmap_name="plasma", name="peaks per\nchannel")
        + facet_grid("Lobe ~ dataset")
        + scale_x_continuous(breaks=[1, 4, 8, 13, 30, 50, 80])
        + labs(
            x="peak centre frequency (Hz)",
            y="peak size (log-power height above aperiodic)",
            title="Peak size vs centre frequency per lobe (count per channel)",
        )
        + theme_bw()
        + theme(figure_size=(9, 12), plot_title=element_text(size=11))
    )


size_freq_lobe_fig = plot_peak_size_frequency_by_lobe(all_peaks, channel_band)

        fig_dir / f"peak_size_vs_frequency_by_lobe.{ext}",
        width=9, height=12, dpi=150, verbose=False,
    )
```

#### Cross-modal overlap before and after aperiodic correction

Removing the aperiodic component changes the cross-modal picture, and the change depends on how the oscillatory residual is defined. We computed the per-lobe oscillatory spectrum in 2 Hz bins under four extractors — the detrended residual and the modelled (specparam-peak) power, each in a log and a linear form — and compared modalities with a subject-clustered bootstrap (per-lobe mean ± 95% CI, @fig-residual-state) and a frequency cluster-permutation test (Maris-Oostenveld, resampling whole subjects) that controls the family-wise error across frequency (@fig-residual-diff).

```{python}
#| label: imports-lobe
from pesco import config, store, crossmodal
from plotnine import (
    geom_hline,
    geom_line,
    geom_ribbon,
)

DB_PATH = PROJECT_DIR / "data/interim/analysis.duckdb"

BIN_WIDTH = 2.0
B = 2000
LOBE_ORDER_FULL = ["Occipital", "Parietal", "Frontal", "Temporal", "Insula"]
EXTRACTORS = {  # column in feat -> display label (ordered)
    "resid_log": "residual · log",
    "resid_lin": "residual · linear",
    "mod_log": "modelled · log",
    "mod_lin": "modelled · linear",
}
EXTRACTOR_ORDER = list(EXTRACTORS.values())
PARAMS_HASH = store.params_hash(
    config.SPECPARAM_SETTINGS, config.FREQ_RANGE, config.SELECTED_MODE
)
```

```{python}
#| label: load-and-extract
con = store.open_db(DB_PATH)
features = store.load(con, "features", PARAMS_HASH)
channels_lobe = store.load(con, "channels", PARAMS_HASH)[
    ["channel", "dataset", "subject", "Lobe"]
]
con.close()

feat = features.merge(channels_lobe, on=["channel", "dataset"], how="left")
psd = 10.0 ** feat["log_psd"]
psd_ap = 10.0 ** feat["ap_log"]
total = feat.assign(psd=psd).groupby(["dataset", "channel"])["psd"].transform("sum")

feat["resid_log"] = feat["log_psd"] - feat["ap_log"]
feat["resid_lin"] = (psd - psd_ap) / total
feat["mod_log"] = feat["peak_log"]
feat["mod_lin"] = (psd_ap * (10.0 ** feat["peak_log"] - 1.0)) / total
```

```{python}
#| label: binned-matrices
def binned_matrix(feat, dataset, col):
    """channel × bin matrix for one modality/extractor, + subject/lobe per row."""
    sub = feat.loc[feat["dataset"] == dataset, ["channel", "freq", col]]
    wide = sub.pivot(index="channel", columns="freq", values=col).sort_index(axis=1)
    centers, binned = crossmodal.bin_spectrum(
        wide.columns.to_numpy(float), wide.to_numpy(float), BIN_WIDTH
    )
    meta = channels_lobe[channels_lobe["dataset"] == dataset].set_index("channel")
    return {
        "centers": centers,
        "M": binned,
        "subject": meta.loc[wide.index, "subject"].to_numpy(),
        "lobe": meta.loc[wide.index, "Lobe"].to_numpy(),
    }


mats = {
    (col, ds): binned_matrix(feat, ds, col)
    for col in EXTRACTORS
    for ds in config.DATASETS
}
centers = mats[("resid_log", config.DATASETS[0])]["centers"]
```

```{python}
#| label: bootstrap-state
state_rows = []
for col, label in EXTRACTORS.items():
    for ds in config.DATASETS:
        d = mats[(col, ds)]
        for lobe in LOBE_ORDER_FULL:
            rows = d["lobe"] == lobe
            if rows.sum() == 0:
                continue
            point, lo, hi = crossmodal.cluster_bootstrap_cell_means(
                d["M"][rows], d["subject"][rows], B=B, seed=3
            )
            state_rows.append(
                pd.DataFrame(
                    {
                        "extractor": label,
                        "dataset": ds,
                        "Lobe": lobe,
                        "freq": d["centers"],
                        "mean": point,
                        "lo": lo,
                        "hi": hi,
                    }
                )
            )
state = pd.concat(state_rows, ignore_index=True)
state["extractor"] = pd.Categorical(state["extractor"], EXTRACTOR_ORDER, ordered=True)
state["dataset"] = pd.Categorical(state["dataset"], config.DATASETS, ordered=True)
state["Lobe"] = pd.Categorical(state["Lobe"], LOBE_ORDER_FULL, ordered=True)
```

```{python}
#| label: cluster-permutation
# Maris–Oostenveld cluster permutation across frequency, per (extractor, lobe).
# Exchangeable unit = subject: per-bin Welch t between iEEG-patient and HD-subject
# means, thresholded into frequency clusters whose mass is tested against a
# subject-relabelling null. Controls family-wise error over the ~40 bins.
perm_rows = []
for col, label in EXTRACTORS.items():
    a, b = mats[(col, "iEEG atlas")], mats[(col, "source HD-EEG")]
    for lobe in LOBE_ORDER_FULL:
        ra, rb = a["lobe"] == lobe, b["lobe"] == lobe
        _, A = crossmodal.subject_means(a["M"][ra], a["subject"][ra])
        _, Bm = crossmodal.subject_means(b["M"][rb], b["subject"][rb])
        if A.shape[0] < 2 or Bm.shape[0] < 2:
            continue
        res = crossmodal.cluster_permutation_freq(A, Bm, n_perm=2000, seed=3)
        perm_rows.append(
            pd.DataFrame(
                {
                    "extractor": label,
                    "Lobe": lobe,
                    "freq": a["centers"],
                    "t": res["t_obs"],
                    "significant": res["sig"],
                }
            )
        )
diff = pd.concat(perm_rows, ignore_index=True)
diff["extractor"] = pd.Categorical(diff["extractor"], EXTRACTOR_ORDER, ordered=True)
diff["Lobe"] = pd.Categorical(diff["Lobe"], LOBE_ORDER_FULL, ordered=True)
diff.to_csv(
    PROJECT_DIR / "data/interim/specparam_model_selection/"
    "lobe_residual_rhythmic_diff_clusterperm.csv",
    index=False,
)
```

The **modelled** rhythmic power — the measure that does not depend on the accuracy of the aperiodic fit — shows iEEG and HD-EEG differing in a contiguous beta/low-gamma cluster (~25-48 Hz, iEEG higher) across most lobes, and a parietal alpha cluster (~10-12 Hz) where HD-EEG is higher; occipital high-gamma is again higher in iEEG. The **detrended residual** reproduces the beta excess but adds a broad high-frequency cluster (~55-80 Hz) in which HD-EEG appears systematically higher than iEEG across every lobe. This high-frequency block is present in the residual but absent from the modelled measure, identifying it as aperiodic-tail/noise leakage rather than a rhythm — exactly the conflation that @castanheira2025QuantifyingRhythmicArrhythmic predict for detrended spectra.
<!-- REVIEW: "exactly the conflation that ... predict" overstates the match. "the kind of conflation ... describe" is safer. -->
 The log and linear residuals agree on the sign and location of the clusters but differ in magnitude, as expected from their different units.

We therefore read the modelled-peak comparison as the substantive cross-modal result: the rhythms that survive aperiodic separation correspond across modalities chiefly in the alpha band, with a beta/low-gamma offset, whereas the apparent high-frequency cross-modal difference in the subtraction residual is an artefact of the aperiodic background rather than a difference in oscillatory activity.
